considered.name: Debt Repayment Trajectory At Cheap Value
considered.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(ebitda, ADD(SUB(ADD(MUL(prcc_f, csho), dltt), che), dlc))), WINSOR(TREND(RATIO(SUB(dltr, dltis), at), 5), 1))
considered.hypothesis: For a cheaply valued and leveraged business, the multi-year path of debt repayment is the financing decision that matters most: steadily rising net repayment transfers enterprise value from creditors to shareholders and removes the risk that justified the discount, whereas a steadily rising reliance on new borrowing is the path toward the distress the market fears.
considered.reasoning: Every trajectory result so far has used a flow dominated by shareholder payout, so this isolates whether the mechanism is shareholder orientation specifically or a general policy of claim retirement — a question the level-based tests could not answer because levels of debt flows were absorbed by the investment factor. It uses only cash-flow-statement debt items, giving it a failure mode independent of the payout family and a clean interpretation either way.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Accelerating Capital Return When Cheap
considered.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(ebitda, ADD(SUB(ADD(MUL(prcc_f, csho), dltt), che), dlc))), WINSOR(ACCEL(RATIO(SUB(SUB(ADD(prstkc, dvc), sstk), SUB(dltis, dltr)), at)), 1))
considered.hypothesis: If the market underreacts to gradual shifts in shareholder orientation, it should underreact most where the shift is speeding up: a cheap firm whose capital return is not merely rising but rising at an increasing rate is in the early, least-recognised phase of a policy change, and the second derivative should lead the first.
considered.reasoning: Position, level-deviation and slope have all now been tested, and acceleration is the one remaining temporal object in this family — it is distinct because a firm can have a strong five-year slope that is flattening (late, already priced) or a modest slope that is steepening (early, unpriced). It also requires fewer years of history than the five-point trend, so it should recover part of the coverage the winning signal gives up.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Payout Mix Shift Toward Buybacks When Cheap
considered.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(ebitda, ADD(SUB(ADD(MUL(prcc_f, csho), dltt), che), dlc))), WINSOR(TREND(RATIO(SUB(prstkc, dvt), at), 5), 1))
considered.hypothesis: Dividends are a price-insensitive commitment while repurchases are a price-contingent investment in the firm's own shares, so a cheap company that has spent five years steadily shifting its payout mix away from dividends and toward buybacks is revealing a strengthening view that its stock is the best available use of cash — whereas a cheap firm drifting the other way is signalling that management sees no such opportunity.
considered.reasoning: This is not a rescaling of an existing signal: the financing object is the *composition* of payout rather than its total, and the archive's one composition test was measured in levels, where it produced a suggestive alpha (0.021, t 1.58) alongside a completely flat cross-sectional slope (0.20). Since the trend transformation converted every other level-based leg in this archive from weak to strong evidence, applying it to the one channel that showed abnormal return without a slope is the highest-information use of the final slot, and it directly tests whether the trajectory mechanism is about the amount returned or about the form in which it is returned.
considered.author: proposer

critic_notes.target_name: Conviction Value Net Payout
critic_notes.rationale: This is an equal-weight rank blend of two well-documented published anomalies (book-to-market and net repurchase/payout yield) with no genuine interaction — SUMRANK is additive, so it cannot test the stated "double-confirmation" conditioning story and amounts to a trivial rediscovery.

critic_notes.target_name: Financing Signed Cheapness
critic_notes.rationale: The sign flip mechanically places expensive net issuers (very negative z-score × −1) in the long leg, which directly contradicts the overvaluation logic the proposal invokes, and the binary SIGN of a near-zero prstkc−sstk difference makes the moderator extremely noisy for the many firms with small offsetting option-related issuance.

critic_notes.target_name: Enterprise Yield Capital Return
critic_notes.rationale: EBITDA/EV and net total external financing are each established published anomalies and their SUMRANK is again purely additive, plus the "whole-capital" claim is undercut by scaling the financing leg by equity market cap rather than enterprise value.

critic_notes.target_name: Persistent Buyback Value
critic_notes.rationale: This is a cosmetic three-year-smoothing variant of the first proposal in the same batch and overlaps directly with the known composite-issuance anomaly, so it adds a horizon tweak rather than a distinct economic mechanism.

critic_notes.target_name: Overvaluation Timed Issuance
critic_notes.rationale: The multiplicative structure is a legitimate conditional rather than an additive blend, but the stated reasoning is wrong about the expression's direction (a non-negative RANK multiplier makes expensive issuers the most *positive*, not most negative, scores) and the mechanical consequence is that the long leg is dominated by expensive repurchasers rather than cheap ones; additionally, raw csho growth is not split-adjusted and will generate spurious dilution readings.

critic_notes.target_name: Cash Yield External Finance Gap
critic_notes.rationale: The second leg is essentially Bradshaw-Richardson-Sloan net external financing scaled by assets and the first is standard cash-flow-to-price, so this is an additive recombination of two known anomalies with no conditioning and heavy redundancy with the other five proposals in this batch.

critic_notes.target_name: Value Payout Amplification Interaction
critic_notes.rationale: This is effectively a rediscovery of the archive's "Book Equity Retired Per Market Dollar" (BM × net-repurchase-yield, up to centering and scaling), and the centering claim is doubly flawed — cross-products of skewed characteristics are not orthogonal to their main effects in practice, and the construction places overvalued net issuers in the *long* leg, which contradicts the stated undervaluation mechanism.

critic_notes.target_name: Buyback Surprise Among Cheap Firms
critic_notes.rationale: Replacing the persistent payout level with a year-over-year change in net repurchase intensity is a genuine, well-motivated design change (news vs. steady state) rather than a rescaling of the archive signals, the asset-scaling choice sensibly avoids price contamination of both legs, and the expression matches the hypothesis and sign.

critic_notes.target_name: Financing Response To Valuation Shock
critic_notes.rationale: The one-year change in book-to-market is just a noisy inverse of past return, so this reproduces the archive's "Contrarian Buyback At Own Valuation Low" (buyback conditioned on the firm's own valuation decline) with a shorter lookback and a different flow scaler — a horizon variant, not a new channel.

critic_notes.target_name: Industry Relative Cheap Self Funded Payout
critic_notes.rationale: A single, cleanly isolated design change (industry-demeaning the EV multiple in the strongest generation-0 signal) that is well motivated by the industry-level nature of enterprise multiples and diagnostic of whether the missing alpha is a value/industry tilt, though it remains an incremental refinement rather than a new mechanism.

critic_notes.target_name: Cheap Firm Buyback Over Dividend Tilt
critic_notes.rationale: Payout *composition* conditioned on cheapness is a defensibly distinct channel from the archive's payout-level interactions, but the claim that prstkc−dvt is "payout-neutral" is overstated — it is a difference of yields still dominated by repurchase intensity, and it drops issuance entirely, so the mix interpretation is looser than advertised.

critic_notes.target_name: Net Cash Valuation Repurchase
critic_notes.rationale: Net-cash-to-price is a valuation proxy genuinely distinct from book-to-market (book equity blends cash with operating assets), and the interaction is economically necessary rather than decorative since cash-rich firms are otherwise a weak-return group, giving this a real chance of escaping the HML absorption that flattened the archive alphas.

critic_notes.target_name: Industry Neutral Both Legs Capital Return
critic_notes.rationale: A defensible second-order neutralization of the archive's best signal with a coherent peer-deviation story, but the stated claim that IND_ADJ "preserves its sign and magnitude" is factually wrong — demeaning flips the sign of low-but-nonzero payout firms in high-payout industries, so the tails will be populated differently than the hypothesis describes, and the incremental value over the existing industry-ranked version is modest.

critic_notes.target_name: Gross Capital Return At Cheap Enterprise Value
critic_notes.rationale: Stripping the debt term leaves gross net-payout-yield interacted with an EV multiple, i.e. essentially the published net payout yield / shareholder yield anomaly crossed with value, and as a deliberate one-term deletion from an archive signal it is a diagnostic ablation rather than a new hypothesis worth a slot.

critic_notes.target_name: Cash Conversion Enterprise Yield Capital Return
critic_notes.rationale: Swapping EBITDA for operating cash flow in the valuation leg is a single-knob change, but it is economically motivated by the signal's own "internally funded" claim and is testable against a fixed comparator; watch coverage, since the archive's oancf-based signal dropped to 0.086 and its evidence was the weakest of the family.

critic_notes.target_name: Dividend Commitment Increase At Cheap Enterprise Value
critic_notes.rationale: This is the only proposal introducing a genuinely different information channel (sticky-commitment signaling rather than opportunistic timing) into the working valuation frame, though dividend-change signaling is a long-studied effect and DELTA(dvt)/at will be near-zero for most firms, so dispersion and the fate of the archive's failed change-based buyback signal are real concerns.

critic_notes.target_name: Sustained Claim Contraction At Cheap Enterprise Value
critic_notes.rationale: Cumulating three years of the same construct is a legitimate response to the diagnosed imprecision (t=1.42 on a meaningful alpha) and yields a falsifiable persistent-versus-news test, but a multi-year cumulative net-issuance measure edges toward the known composite-issuance anomaly and remains a horizon variant of the same family.

critic_notes.target_name: Financing Direction Purity At Cheap Book Value
critic_notes.rationale: The bounded direction-of-financing ratio is the most structurally distinct construction here and plausibly decouples the interaction from CMA/size loadings that flattened the yield-scaled versions, though including dvt in the denominator contradicts the stated "share retirement versus issuance purity" interpretation by penalizing dividend payers, and firms with near-zero gross activity may create unstable or missing observations.

critic_notes.target_name: Within Cheap Capital Return Conditional
critic_notes.rationale: The hard-indicator restriction genuinely converts the archive's incumbent into a within-stratum comparison that neutralizes the HML/CMA gradient the archive diagnosed, and the expression matches the hypothesis, though it remains the same two legs as "Self Funded Payout At Cheap Enterprise Value" with only the conditioning weight changed, and the 70% mass of exact zeros will make the middle of the sort degenerate.

critic_notes.target_name: Within Expensive Net Issuance Conditional
critic_notes.rationale: The sign convention is internally consistent (long = expensive repurchasers, short = expensive issuers) and it is a defensible structural response to the wrong-signed +0.048 alpha of the archive's rich-valuation issuance signal, but the underlying content is close to the well-documented net-issuance/market-timing anomaly and the pairing with Signal 1 is more of a diagnostic split than a new mechanism.

critic_notes.target_name: Cheap Growing Firm Capital Return
critic_notes.rationale: Multiplying a nonnegative growth rank into a signed payout term makes the short leg "cheap, fast-growing net issuers," which is essentially the asset-growth/external-financing anomaly restated rather than a neutralization of CMA, and the long leg (cheap + high growth + large self-funded payout) is a rare corner likely to produce unstable portfolio composition.

critic_notes.target_name: Cheap Firm Financing Policy Stability
critic_notes.rationale: The expression is internally inconsistent with its hypothesis: since IND_RANK is nonnegative and NEG(VOL) is nonpositive, the maximum values (~0) are attained by expensive firms regardless of financing volatility, so the long leg is dominated by high-multiple names rather than the intended cheap-and-stable firms, and financing volatility is also heavily confounded with size and general firm volatility.

critic_notes.target_name: Drawdown Repurchase Conviction
critic_notes.rationale: The multiplicative structure is coherent here (firms near their highs correctly collapse to the uninformative middle) and a pure price-history conditioner is not spanned by FF5, but the annual-frequency 5-year drawdown is a coarse conditioner and the design sits very close to the archive's already-tested "Contrarian Buyback At Own Valuation Low," so the incremental content is modest.

critic_notes.target_name: Capital Return Per Sales Dollar At Cheap Value
critic_notes.rationale: This is a denominator swap on the archive's incumbent signal — a cosmetic variant in construction even though the stated motivation (removing price from both legs) is a legitimate diagnostic — and scaling by sales introduces its own distortions for low-sales, financial, and pre-revenue firms that a 1% winsor will not fully control.

critic_notes.target_name: Sign Decomposed Two Sided Capital Signal
critic_notes.rationale: The ADD(x,|x|)/SUB(x,|x|) decomposition correctly isolates positive and negative payout parts and the sign structure genuinely matches the stated asymmetric hypothesis (cheap repurchasers long, rich issuers short), but since IND_RANK(NEG(y)) is essentially 1−IND_RANK(y) the whole thing reduces to a piecewise-linear reweighting of the same incumbent interaction that has repeatedly failed to produce FF5 alpha, so the expected gain is modest.

critic_notes.target_name: Convex Cheapness Weighted Capital Return
critic_notes.rationale: Squaring a [0,1] rank weight is a monotone rescaling of the incumbent's valuation leg that will produce a signal correlated near-unity in rank with the existing "Industry Relative Cheap Self Funded Payout," making this the textbook cosmetic variant the objective warns against rather than a new mechanism.

critic_notes.target_name: Cheap Given Profitability Capital Return
critic_notes.rationale: The construction is internally consistent and the "cheap conditional on profitability" moderator is a defensible new conditioning variable, but the claimed orthogonality to HML/RMW is overstated — with ebitda in both numerators, rank(ebitda/EV) − rank(ebitda/at) collapses approximately to a ranking of assets-to-enterprise-value, i.e. another value measure, so the alpha-leakage argument in the reasoning should not be trusted.

critic_notes.target_name: Cash Backed Earnings Behind The Buyback
critic_notes.rationale: Accrual quality (ib − oancf) as a credibility filter on the financing signal is a genuinely new economic dimension for this archive, the nonnegative rank weight preserves the intended sign structure, and while the standalone accrual anomaly is well known, the interaction — buybacks funded by real cash versus accrual-inflated earnings — is not a direct rediscovery; the main risk is the usual triple-product dilution.

critic_notes.target_name: Rank Stabilized Capital Return At Cheap Value
critic_notes.rationale: Swapping a winsorized flow for its centered cross-sectional rank is a pure distributional robustness tweak with no new economic content, and it additionally destroys the meaningful distinction between zero and near-zero financing activity by spreading the large mass of inactive firms across the rank scale.

critic_notes.target_name: Cash Flow Capped Buyback At Cheap Value
critic_notes.rationale: The MIN cap is a structurally different implementation of funding capacity than the incumbent's linear net-debt subtraction, but by construction the short leg becomes populated by low- and negative-operating-cash-flow firms irrespective of any financing action, so much of the resulting spread is a cheapness-times-cash-profitability composite that RMW in the FF5 regression is likely to absorb.

critic_notes.target_name: All Cash Credibility Capital Return
critic_notes.rationale: A legitimate but incremental ablation that simply multiplies two existing archive signals (the oancf/EV multiple and the accrual-gap weight), and because both legs are driven by the same oancf term the "credibility" weight and the "cheapness" weight are partly redundant, so a positive result will be hard to attribute to the stated mechanism.

critic_notes.target_name: Persistent Earnings Quality Capital Return
critic_notes.rationale: This is the generation-4 winner with a three-year moving average bolted onto the conditioning weight — a measurement-horizon tweak with no new economic content, precisely the cosmetic variant the objective warns against.

critic_notes.target_name: Stable Earnings Backing The Buyback
critic_notes.rationale: Earnings-volatility conditioning is a genuinely distinct credibility axis from the accrual gap (and from the previously tested financing-volatility weight), and the proposal correctly frames it as a coverage-versus-channel diagnostic for whether the gen-4 alpha was a sample-restriction artifact.

critic_notes.target_name: Refinancing Risk Filtered Capital Return
critic_notes.rationale: Maturity structure is a new and economically coherent conditioning variable, clearly distinct from the total-leverage weight already tested, available at full coverage, and it makes a falsifiable claim about why some cheap repurchasers fail.

critic_notes.target_name: Credibility Weighted Two Sided Capital Signal
critic_notes.rationale: The stacking is internally inconsistent on the short side — multiplying the sign-decomposed score by a positive accrual-quality rank in [0,1] shrinks low-credibility issuers toward zero, i.e. shorts them *less*, which contradicts both the stated hypothesis and the treatment of issuers in the sixth proposal — and it also mechanically inherits the 0.078 coverage penalty without a new mechanism.

critic_notes.target_name: Cash Burning Issuance At Rich Valuation
critic_notes.rationale: The sign convention is internally consistent, but this is close to a repackaged composite mispricing score (net stock issuance × market-to-book × profitability) that FF5's RMW/CMA largely span, the stated claim that a product of three uniform ranks is "well dispersed" is wrong (it is heavily mass-concentrated near zero, making the long leg an unstable residual), and the raw market-to-book rank misclassifies negative-book-equity firms as cheap.

critic_notes.target_name: Balance Sheet Accrual Credibility Capital Return
critic_notes.rationale: The balance-sheet accrual construction is a legitimate, coverage-restoring alternative measurement of the archive's best-performing credibility channel (0.078 → ~0.11) rather than a pure operator tweak, though it remains an incremental re-measurement of an already-tested mechanism and imports a well-known standalone anomaly (Sloan accruals) as the weight.

critic_notes.target_name: Conjunctive Credibility And Cheapness
critic_notes.rationale: Swapping MUL for MIN on two [0,1] ranks is close to cosmetic — the two combinations are highly rank-correlated — and the MIN-of-two-ranks structure has already been used twice in the archive (Double Confirmation Value Payout, Unlevered Cheap Repurchaser) with weak portfolio evidence, so this is unlikely to diagnose why the three-way product diluted the slope.

critic_notes.target_name: Credibility Certifies The Shareholder Decision
critic_notes.rationale: Dropping the net-debt-issuance term is a directed, economically motivated ablation that cleanly separates "certified equity payout" from "certified total claim contraction," but it is a single-term deletion from an existing signal and the resulting payout leg is close to the published net-payout-yield anomaly, so the incremental information is modest.

critic_notes.target_name: Revenue Multiple Cheapness With Credible Earnings
critic_notes.rationale: Substituting sales-to-EV for EBITDA-to-EV is a genuinely different valuation leg with a coherent rationale (deliberately decorrelating from RMW/HML, which have plausibly absorbed prior spreads) and industry ranking is correctly justified, though coverage will remain pinned near 0.078 by the retained oancf term — the very limitation Signal 1 sets out to fix.

critic_notes.target_name: Payout At Own History High When Cheap
critic_notes.rationale: The five-year within-firm rank is a sensible fix for the noisy one-year payout difference, but the expression is internally inconsistent on the short side: because TS_RANK is strictly non-negative and multiplies a signed payout, a net issuer that is issuing *less* than its own history receives a *more* negative score than one issuing at its five-year extreme, inverting the intended ordering for exactly the firms the hypothesis claims to identify.

critic_notes.target_name: Accrual Inflated Issuance At Rich Enterprise Value
critic_notes.rationale: The three-way rich × accrual-inflated × issuing construction is a distinct combination rather than a rediscovery of the archive's two prior short-side attempts, and the sign convention is internally consistent, but the same non-negative-weight asymmetry places rich, accrual-heavy *repurchasers* in the long leg, and every previous rich-issuance variant produced FF5 alpha of the wrong sign, so the prior is unfavorable.

critic_notes.target_name: Unusual Payout With Credible Earnings
critic_notes.rationale: A legitimate but largely mechanical stacking of the archive's two best components (gen-6 within-firm payout position and gen-4 accrual credibility) that swaps only one factor relative to "Cash Backed Earnings Behind The Buyback," and the triple product plus the drop to 0.078 coverage makes dilution the most likely outcome — acceptable as an additivity test, not as a discovery.

critic_notes.target_name: Fully Within Firm Valuation And Payout Extremes
critic_notes.rationale: Genuinely distinct from "Contrarian Buyback At Own Valuation Low" (which paired a within-firm B/M rank with a cross-sectional payout level), internally consistent in sign, and well-motivated by the diagnosis that the cross-sectional cheapness leg is what FF5 absorbs — though a 5-point annual TS_RANK on the EV multiple is coarse and will be noisy.

critic_notes.target_name: Payout Magnitude Plus Unusualness When Cheap
critic_notes.rationale: This is close to a cosmetic blend of two already-tested financing legs (cross-sectional payout/EV magnitude and within-firm TS_RANK) under an unchanged valuation leg, and SUMRANK-then-ZSCORE will mostly average the two existing signals rather than test a distinct economic mechanism, so the likely result is an interpolation between the incumbent slope and the gen-6 alpha with no new information.

critic_notes.target_name: Cardinal Payout Deviation From Own Norm
critic_notes.rationale: A clean single-variable ablation (ordinal vs cardinal within-firm deviation) that is defensible as a design test, but it is close in spirit to the already-failed "Buyback Surprise Among Cheap Firms" (one-year DELTA of the same flow, fmb_tstat 1.27), so the prior on a cardinal-difference measure of a lumpy annual flow succeeding is low.

critic_notes.target_name: Unusual External Capital Raising At Rich Value
critic_notes.rationale: The expected sign correctly matches the expression's direction (expensive × unusually-high gross raising scores high and is predicted to underperform), the gross-raising construction is a substantive rather than cosmetic departure from prior netted issuance legs, and it addresses the diagnosed failure of every earlier short-side attempt; the main caveat is that the long leg becomes "expensive firms that rarely raise," whose economics the hypothesis leaves unspecified.

critic_notes.target_name: Improving Capital Return Trajectory When Cheap
critic_notes.rationale: Slope through the range is a genuinely different temporal object from position within it or the failed multi-year TS_SUM of levels, the hypothesis (gradual shareholder-orientation shift is underreacted to) is economically coherent, and the sign direction is consistent — though a five-observation OLS trend on a lumpy annual financing flow is statistically fragile and coverage will suffer.

critic_notes.target_name: Payout Regime Shift When Cheap
critic_notes.rationale: The archive already contains two highly correlated estimators of exactly this "policy shift" object at the same valuation conditioning — the 5-year OLS trend (alpha 0.038, t 3.76) and current-level-minus-5yr-MA (alpha 0.036, t 3.27) — so a three-year-versus-lagged-three-year average difference is a third smoothing of the same construct and is very likely to be a cosmetic estimator variant rather than new economic information.

critic_notes.target_name: Two Sided Payout Trajectory
critic_notes.rationale: The positive/negative-part decomposition is correctly constructed (ADD(x,ABS(x)) isolates improvers weighted by cheapness, SUB(x,ABS(x)) isolates deteriorators weighted by richness) and the expected positive sign follows, but the identical decomposition applied to payout levels already underperformed the simple conditional version (alpha 0.010, t 1.12), so the prior that the short-leg re-weighting helps is weak.

critic_notes.target_name: Own Multiple And Own Trajectory
critic_notes.rationale: Combining the two orthogonalizations that each independently improved alpha (within-firm valuation ranking and the trend-measured financing leg) is a coherent test of whether they compound or overlap, though there is a real risk that TS_RANK of the EV multiple mostly picks up the same firm-specific state that a rising payout trend already encodes, making the two legs mechanically correlated.

critic_notes.target_name: Shareholder Payout Trajectory When Cheap
critic_notes.rationale: A clean single-component ablation of the winning signal with a pre-stated interpretive fork in either direction, which is legitimate mechanism testing even if it is low-ambition and its most likely outcome is a modest degradation that merely confirms the debt leg contributes.

critic_notes.target_name: Noise Scaled Payout Trajectory When Cheap
critic_notes.rationale: Dividing a 5-year slope by the 5-year volatility of the same series is numerically unstable — firms with near-zero financing variability (many of them precisely the inactive, uninformative ones) produce explosive ratios that WINSOR at 1% will not adequately tame, and the numerator is itself a component of the denominator, so the ranking risks being driven by degenerate low-dispersion cases rather than by genuine policy conviction.

critic_notes.target_name: Payout Trajectory Beyond Earnings Trajectory
critic_notes.rationale: Purging the profitability cycle from the trajectory directly addresses the legitimate concern that this family is an RMW-spanned recovery bet, but the two raw slopes are differenced without standardization and EBITDA/assets trends are typically far larger in magnitude than net-payout/assets trends, so the composite may end up ranking primarily on declining profitability rather than on discretionary payout expansion.

critic_notes.target_name: Two Sided Payout Deviation From Own Norm
critic_notes.rationale: The construction is internally coherent (positive deviations weighted by cheapness, negative by richness, consistent with a positive sign) and pairs the archive's best structural template with its best-Sharpe measurement, but it is a mechanical crossing of two already-tested archive components rather than a new mechanism, so its incremental information is limited to whether the two-sided weighting generalizes.

critic_notes.target_name: Rising Payout Long Rising Raising Short
critic_notes.rationale: This is the most substantive proposal in the batch — it replaces the short leg's variable rather than reweighting it, the sign algebra checks out (rich firms with rising gross raising receive a negative contribution), and it directly tests whether the short side is about market dependence rather than the negative tail of a netted flow; the main risk is double-loading of firms that both pay out and raise.

critic_notes.target_name: Standardized Payout Trend Beyond Earnings Trend
critic_notes.rationale: This is a monotone rescaling of an existing archive signal, and the archive already contains a common-scale differenced version of exactly this idea ("Payout Unusual Beyond The Earnings Cycle", fmb 1.11, alpha 0.020) whose weak result undercuts the claimed scale-mismatch diagnosis; the change is cosmetic rather than economic.

critic_notes.target_name: Two Sided Trajectory Against Multiple Path
critic_notes.rationale: Sign logic and construction are sound and the both-legs-as-paths framing is a genuinely untried configuration, but like proposal one it is a template-times-base recombination of two archived results, and the earnings-yield trend leg risks becoming a disguised multi-year price-reversal bet rather than a valuation state.

critic_notes.target_name: Debt Repayment Trajectory At Cheap Value
critic_notes.rationale: A clean and diagnostically valuable decomposition — it isolates the debt half of the combined flow whose shareholder half already tested weakly, so either outcome is informative about the mechanism, though it edges toward the well-known debt-issuance/net-external-financing anomaly and the five-point trend on lumpy dltr/dltis will be noisy.

critic_notes.target_name: Accelerating Capital Return When Cheap
critic_notes.rationale: Acceleration is the one untested temporal object in this family and the hypothesis is coherent, but second differences of a lumpy annual payout flow are very noisy, and the claimed coverage gain over the five-year trend is asserted without justification and may not materialize.
